title: When Concealed Links Cannot Be Recovered: A Structural Identifiability Bound and Evaluation Pitfalls in Offshore Leak Networks
summary: Leaks such as the Panama and Paradise Papers expose large networks of offshore entities, and they invite an obvious question for network learning. Can the relations these structures are built to hide---above all, who beneficially owns what---be recovered from the public part of the leak by link prediction? We argue that the answer is mostly no, and that the analyses which suggest otherwise are measuring the wrong thing. Our main result is a distribution-free identifiability bound. For any recovery rule that respects graph isomorphism, and that covers every topological link-prediction score…
